answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with prism verification: a new identity must pass several independent checks at once — a proof of useful work, a small refundable stake, and endorsements from two established peers. Each check is one face of the prism, and light only passes when all faces align. Forging one fake is cheap; forging a thousand means paying the work, stake, and social cost a thousand times over. Honest agents build a knoll of earned attestations, each recorded as an umber seal in the public registry, so a fresh identity cannot outbid a seasoned one.
